description: Analyze an image and return its probable real-world location. Returns ranked coordinates with a confidence score and the visual evidence chain the analysis used (architecture, signage, vegetation, terrain, lighting). No EXIF or GPS required. Capped at 20 analyses an hour across all Oceanir analysis tools, and a connected app is limited to depth 2 (an agent token with maximum depth 3 can use depth 3). Reads the scene only (architecture, signage, terrain, vegetation), never the people in it. No face recognition, no biometric identification, no person matching. It answers where an image was taken, never who is in it, and must not be used to locate or track a person.

depth.description: Analysis depth. 1 = Surface (region scan, 1 credit). 2 = Standard (ranked candidates with evidence, 2 credits). 3 = Forensic (deeper reasoning and contradiction checks, 10 credits).

image_url.description: Public HTTPS URL to the image to analyze.

scope.description: The location being claimed. Oceanir treats this as a search boundary and never as evidence: it can only narrow the search, never raise confidence, and the model will reject it outright on hard image-legible contradiction (signage in an impossible script, the wrong driving side, a landmark that is elsewhere).

captured_at.description: When the image is CLAIMED to have been taken. Optional, and worth sending whenever the claim carries a date, because it is the only check here that does not depend on the model's own confidence. A bare date (2026-09-12) returns whether the sun rose at that place at all that day and for how long; at high latitudes that alone can contradict a daylit image outright. A time WITH a UTC offset (2026-09-12T14:30:00-04:00) additionally returns the sun's altitude and compass direction at that moment. A time WITHOUT an offset has its clock time ignored and only its date used: an assumed timezone can turn noon into midnight, so it is never guessed.

radius_km.description: How far from the centre still counts as the claimed place. Defaults to 60km, which covers a metro area.

name: geolocate_image
title: Locate a photo
